sources.title: Along the River During the Qingming Festival (detail of the original scroll showing a wooden arched bridge)
sources.author: Zhang Zeduan, Song dynasty painter

sources.repository: Wikimedia Commons (file page records the source and public-domain tag)

sources.modified: unmodified except Wikimedia Commons' scaled 1280-pixel-wide JPEG rendering of a detail of the scroll
sources.alt: A detail of a Chinese handscroll painted in ink and color on silk: a crowded wooden arched bridge crosses a river; people, market stalls with umbrellas, carts and pack animals fill the street beside it, cargo boats float on the river, and tiled roofs fill the foreground.
sources.credit: Zhang Zeduan, Along the River During the Qingming Festival (detail), early 12th century. Via Wikimedia Commons (public domain).
sources.notes: The scroll is usually dated to the early 12th century and shows daily life and commerce in a Song-dynasty city; the detail shown is one section of a much longer scroll.

sources.alt: A black-and-white woodcut of a printing workshop: two men in the foreground work at a press table, one lifting a tray of type and one inking it with a dabber, while a large wooden screw press stands at the right, stacks of printed sheets lie on a bench in front, and two more workers stand in the background by a window.
